title: Vikings suspend Gerald Alexander for 3 weeks following DWI guilty plea
dek: The Minnesota Vikings suspended assistant coach Gerald Alexander for three weeks without pay following his July 16 guilty plea to third-degree DWI. Alexander was arrested April 26 in Edina after refusing a breathalyzer test. The suspension runs from July 25 through August 13.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Gerald Alexander, hired by the Vikings in February as defensive passing game coordinator/defensive backs, was suspended three weeks without pay after pleading guilty to third-degree DWI on July 16.
bottom_line: Alexander's suspension runs concurrent with the start of Vikings training camp and preseason games. The timing of the discipline, enacted after the guilty plea rather than immediately following the arrest, reflects the team's practice of awaiting legal resolution before administrative action on coaching staff. Watch whether the Vikings' decision to restore him after three weeks holds or whether additional action follows.
body: The Minnesota Vikings suspended assistant coach Gerald Alexander for three weeks without pay following his guilty plea to third-degree DWI, a gross misdemeanor charge. The suspension began Friday, July 25 and concludes August 13, according to ESPN's reporting.

Alexander was stopped in Edina, a Minneapolis suburb, on April 26 and refused a breathalyzer test during the stop, per court documents cited by ESPN. He pleaded guilty on July 16 to the charge and was ordered to pay $603 in fines and fees, complete 48 hours of community service, and serve two years of unsupervised probation, according to ESPN's reporting.

The Vikings hired Alexander in February as defensive passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach, replacing Daronte Jones, who left for the Washington Commanders' defensive coordinator role. Alexander has prior coaching history with Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, having worked together in both Miami and Pittsburgh.

In a statement reported by ESPN, Alexander said: "I take full responsibility for the situation I put myself in and apologize for not meeting the mark. I know it's unacceptable. I understand the suspension and am committed to learning from the matter and ensuring I come back a better version of myself."

The Vikings stated in their announcement, per ESPN, that they "remained in communication with the NFL while awaiting the outcome of the legal process" following the April arrest. Head coach Kevin O'Connell was expected to address the suspension publicly on the day the action was announced.
